archetype.name: Retooling (play-in bubble)
archetype.definition: A team climbing out of a lost season on a respectable defense while its best guard sits, good enough to hang around .500-level company but not yet good enough to beat it consistently.

report.headline: A real defense and Siakam keep Indiana afloat until Haliburton returns
report.take:
Indiana at 5-9 is not last season's 19-63 team, and the gap is mostly on defense. A year ago the Pacers had the 24th-ranked defense, allowing 118.8 points per 100 possessions. This year the DRtg is 114.2, 14th and exactly league average. The offense is where the weight sits: a 111.7 ORtg ranks 22nd, barely better than last season's 110.9, and the Net Rtg of -2.5 ranks 18th. That is a below-average team, but not a bottom-feeder, and the site's 22nd-of-30 placement is about right.

The defining fact is in the backcourt list: Tyrese Haliburton has played four games and is listed Out. In those games he ran a 7.7 BPM on 63.4 TS %, by far the best impact numbers on the roster. Without him the offense runs through Pascal Siakam, who has 300 points on 60.3 TS % at a 28.2 USG %, the 12th-ranked power forward on the site. Behind him there is little shooting. The team hits 32.8% from three (25th), takes fewer threes than the league norm, and has the league's worst ORB % at 21.5, so empty possessions rarely get a second chance.

The record isn't hiding much. W vs Pt Diff is -1, so the margin implies six wins rather than five, and the 29-win pace is close to what the play has earned. The split inside the roster tells you more. The wing rotation is the problem: Aaron Nesmith (-5.1 BPM, -13.1 On-Off) and Kelly Oubre Jr. (-2.9, -11.1) have taken the bulk of small-forward minutes while the team bleeds there. Opposing small forwards are scoring 28.14 points a game, 29th in the league, and taking 24.6% of the points against Indiana compared with a 19.9% league share. Jalen Slawson (+18.6) and Quenton Jackson (+15.7) have been the best On-Off lineups, a small-sample hint that the energy-and-defense pieces fit better than the scorers.

The trajectory is flat. October was a shootout pattern, 116.67 scored and 119.83 allowed. November slowed both ends, to 108.63 and 110.5, and the last five games at 2-3 and -1.4 a game are a touch better than the season line. This is a team waiting on a return rather than a team changing on its own. Until Haliburton is back, expect a sub-.500 team that loses winnable games by single digits.

strengths.title: Defense back to league average
strengths.body: The DRtg of 114.2 sits right on the league mark, a big step from last year's 118.8 and 24th-ranked unit. It is built on keeping opponents away from the basket: Opp Rim Rate of 27 ranks 9th. This looks structural rather than lucky, though opponents' 36.1% from three is a little above the league and could even out in Indiana's favor.

strengths.title: Siakam as the reliable engine
strengths.body: Siakam carries the heaviest load on the team at 28.2 USG % and still scores efficiently at 60.3 TS %, ranking 12th among power forwards. With Haliburton out, he is the one player creating good shots at volume. Expect that to hold, though the burden will be heaviest against defenses like New York's that shut down the position.

strengths.title: Ball security holds up
strengths.body: A 12.9 TOV % ranks 12th, better than the league average, so the offense's problems come from missed shots, not giveaways. That has been an Indiana trait in recent seasons and should last.

concerns.title: Offense without its creator
concerns.body: The 111.7 ORtg ranks 22nd and is barely better than last year's 29th-ranked unit. Shooting is the core problem, at 32.8% from three, 25th. Haliburton's 7.7 BPM in four games is the clearest fix on the roster, but he is listed Out and the sheet gives no timeline. Until he returns, this ceiling stays low.

concerns.title: Wings losing their minutes
concerns.body: The wings grade D-. The two most-used small forwards post deeply negative On-Off numbers, and opposing small forwards are feasting at 28.14 points a game, 29th in the league. This is the leak on both ends. It persists unless the rotation shifts toward Slawson, whose +18.6 On-Off comes in a small sample.

concerns.title: No offensive glass
concerns.body: The ORB % of 21.5 is dead last and the REB % ranks 28th. A poor-shooting team that also concedes almost every miss gives itself no margin. History says this is a long-running trait (21.7% last year, 21.3% in 2024-25), so don't expect it to change.

trend.note: October games were high-scoring losses, and November slowed both ends without changing the result much. The last five, at 2-3, are marginally better than the season line but still below .500.

weekAhead.headline: Four games, three against top-ten Net Rtg teams
weekAhead.body:
This is the hardest stretch of the young season. Houston arrives at 11-3, second on the site, with A+ wings and frontcourt and the 2nd-best ORB %, a direct hit on Indiana's worst number. New York and Oklahoma City both bring top-five defenses (DRtg 108.4 and 108.7), and those two games come on consecutive days, with the Knicks on the road. That leaves little rest for a short rotation.

The best chance is Cleveland on the road. The Cavaliers are 7-7 with a 20th-ranked defense, and they get worked over by centers (22.71 points and 16.36 rebounds a game to the position). A 1-3 week would be par. Two wins would say the defense travels.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's offensive glass
keyMatchups.body: Houston rebounds 32.4% of its own misses, 2nd in the league, against an Indiana team ranked last on its own glass. The Rockets also score efficiently at 122.3 ORtg. If Indiana can't finish possessions with a defensive rebound, this one gets away early.

keyMatchups.title: Zubac and Huff at Cleveland
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland allows the most rebounds to centers in the league and the 26th-most points. This is the week's clearest opening for Indiana's bigs, and Jay Huff's 66.1 TS % suggests he can cash it in.

keyMatchups.title: Siakam into the Knicks wall
keyMatchups.body: New York holds power forwards 7.69 points below their own averages, the best mark in the league. That points straight at Siakam, who is Indiana's offense. Indiana beat the Knicks 106-104 at home last week, but that was in Indianapolis; this one is on the road.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Nembhard (day-to-day) and any Haliburton news change the backcourt, because without both the offense has to run almost entirely through Siakam against three elite defenses.

restOfSeason.body:
The underlying numbers describe a team a little better than its record: the margin implies six wins, not five, and a league-average defense is a real floor. The offense is the limit. Without Haliburton, the shooting and rebounding profile points to an ORtg stuck in the low 110s. That makes a 30-something-win team that lives near the play-in line in a Central division where Milwaukee and Chicago are struggling. A healthy Haliburton for a long stretch is the one swing large enough to push this toward .500. I'd put the range at 30 to 37 wins, with the high end needing him back by midseason.

The defense should mostly hold, though the 14th-ranked DRtg also benefits from keeping opponents out of the paint more than from stopping them once there. The wing rotation is the part to fix. If Slawson's minutes grow at Nesmith's and Oubre's expense, the small-forward bleeding could ease.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting regressing toward league average

confidence.note: Only 14 games, and the star's availability is unknown. But the margin and record agree, and the defensive change from last year is large.
